What is the body's largest organ?

The skin is the body's largest organ! It protects the body, helps control temperature, and lets us feel touch.

Ano ang pinakamalaking organ ng katawan?

Ang balat ang pinakamalaking organ ng katawan! Pinoprotektahan nito ang katawan, tumutulong sa pagkontrol ng temperatura, at ginagawang mararamdaman natin ang hipo.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakadako nga organ sa lawas?

Ang panit mao ang pinakadako nga organ sa lawas! Manalipod kini sa lawas, motabang sa pagkontrol sa temperatura, ug motugot kanato nga makabati sa paghikap.

copy.tl: Ang paraw na may dalawang katig ay nagpapalawak ng base at nagpapababa ng sentro ng grabidad, kaya hindi nagkakabalegtad ang bangka sa malakas na alon!
copy.bis: Ang paraw nga adunay duha ka katig nagpalapad sa base ug nagpababa sa sentro sa grabidad, aron dili mabaliktad ang bangka sa mabangis nga alon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Venom is made inside special glands in an animal's body

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage

Where does an animal's venom come from?

Venom is made inside special glands in an animal's body — snakes, for example, have venom glands near their fangs.
copy.tl:
Saan nanggagaling ang kamandag ng hayop?

Ginagawa ang kamandag sa loob ng espesyal na glandula sa katawan ng hayop — sa ahas, malapit ito sa kanyang mga ngipin.
copy.bis:
Asa naggikan ang kamandag sa hayop?

Ang kamandag gihimo sulod sa espesyal nga glandula sa lawas sa hayop — sa bitin, duol kini sa iyang mga ngipon.

copy.en: Many venomous animals use their venom to paralyze prey first, so it cannot escape before being eaten.
copy.tl: Maraming hayop na may kamandag ang gumagamit nito para paralisahin muna ang biktima, para hindi ito makatakas bago kainin.
copy.bis: Daghang hayop nga adunay kamandag mogamit niini aron paralisahon una ang biktima, aron dili kini makaikyas sa dili pa kan-on.

copy.en:
What happens after a Venus flytrap catches an insect?

After the trap closes, the Venus flytrap slowly digests the insect over several days and absorbs its nutrients.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari matapos madakip ng Venus flytrap ang insekto?

Pagkasara ng bitag, dahan-dahang tinutunaw ng Venus flytrap ang insekto sa loob ng ilang araw at sinisipsip ang sustansya nito.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo human madakop sa Venus flytrap ang insekto?

Human masira ang bitag, hinay-hinay nga tunawon sa Venus flytrap ang insekto sulod sa pipila ka adlaw ug suyupon ang sustansiya niini.

copy.en:
Why does Venus have the longest day?

Venus has the longest day of about 243 Earth days because it spins so, so slowly!
copy.tl:
Bakit ang Venus ang may pinakamahabang araw?

Ang Venus ang may pinakamahabang araw na halos 243 araw ng Mundo, dahil napakabagal nitong umikot!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ang Venus adunay pinakatas-on nga adlaw?

Ang Venus adunay pinakatas-on nga adlaw nga mga 243 ka adlaw sa Yuta, kay hinay kaayo kini motuyok!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition

copy.en: Venus is closer to the Sun than Earth, so it only appears before sunrise or after sunset. That’s why we call it the 'morning star' or 'evening star'!
copy.tl: Mas malapit ang Venus sa Araw kaysa Earth, kaya makikita lang ito bago mag-umaga o pagkatapos ng sunset. Kaya naman tinatawag itong 'morning star' o 'evening star'!
copy.bis: Mas duol ang Venus sa Adlaw kaysa Yuta, busa makita lang kini sa wala pa mosidlak o pagkahuman sa sunset. Mao nga gitawag kini og 'morning star' o 'evening star'!

copy.bis: Ang siyudad sa Pompeii sa Italya nalumpag! Nahitabo kini dihang mibuto ang Bulkang Vesuvius niadtong tuig AD 79.

copy.bis: Ang rattan o uway usa ka nanaka nga palma sa mga lasang sa Pilipinas nga gigamit sa paghimo og muwebles.

Why 'slow the spread' of COVID-19?

It spread too fast, sickening many at once. People used distance and lockdowns to slow it down, keeping hospitals from running out of beds and doctors.
copy.tl:
Bakit sinubukang 'pabagalin ang pagkalat' ng COVID-19?

Kapag napakabilis kumalat ang COVID-19, sabay-sabay na nagkasakit ang napakaraming tao at nauubusan ng kama at doktor ang ospital — kaya ginamit ang distansya at lockdown para pabagalin ito at hindi agad mapuno ang ospital.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga gisulayan ang 'pagpahinay sa pagkatap' sa COVID-19?

Kung paspas kaayo mikatap ang COVID-19, dungan nga nagsakit ang daghang tawo ug nahutdan og higdaanan ug doktor ang ospital — mao nga gigamit ang distansya ug lockdown aron mahinay kini ug dili dayon mapuno ang ospital.

Where do new viruses come from?

Many new viruses, even the one behind COVID-19, are believed to have jumped from animals to people first. That's why we must care for nature and avoid close contact with wild animals.
copy.tl:
Saan nagmumula ang mga bagong virus?

Maraming bagong virus, kahit ang nagdulot ng COVID-19, ay pinaniniwalaang unang galing sa hayop bago tumalon sa tao. Kaya mahalaga ang pag-aalaga sa kalikasan at pag-iwas sa ligaw na hayop.
copy.bis:
Asa naggikan ang mga bag-ong virus?

Daghang bag-ong virus, bisan ang hinungdan sa COVID-19, gituohan nga unang gikan sa hayop una milukso sa tawo. Mao nga importante ang pag-atiman sa kinaiyahan ug paglikay sa ihalas nga hayop.

copy.tl: Karaniwang binubuo ang virus ng genetic material (DNA o RNA) na nababalot ng isang patong na protina na tinatawag na capsid.
copy.bis: Ang virus kasagaran gilangkuban og genetic material (DNA o RNA) nga giputos sa usa ka sapaw nga protina nga gitawag og capsid.

How do cells warn each other about a virus?

An infected cell releases proteins called interferons that warn nearby cells to prepare for attack — an important first defense against viruses!
copy.tl:
Paano nagbababala ang selula tungkol sa virus?

Ang isang nahawahang cell ay naglalabas ng mga protinang tinatawag na interferon na nagbababala sa mga kalapit na cell na maghanda sa atake — isang mahalagang unang linya ng depensa laban sa virus!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagpahibalo sa selula bahin sa virus?

Ang usa ka nahawahang cell nagpagawas og mga protina nga gitawag og interferon nga nagpahibalo sa mga silingang cell nga moandam para sa pag-atake — usa ka importanteng unang linya sa depensa batok sa virus!

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses viruses not being cells, but does not address unicellular vs multicellular organisms (e.g., bacteria vs humans). It does not directly support recognizing that some organisms are single-celled and others are multi-celled.

copy.en:
Why isn't a virus considered a cell?

It lacks parts like ribosomes or organelles — the things it would need to carry out its own metabolism.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi selula ang virus?

Wala itong mga bahagi gaya ng ribosome o organelle na kailangan para sa sariling metabolismo.
copy.bis:
Nganong dili selula ang virus?

Wala kini mga bahin sama sa ribosome o organelle nga gikinahanglan alang sa kaugalingong metabolismo.

copy.bis: Nagpuyo ang Visayan warty pig sa gagmayng grupo — sagad usa ka inahan ug ang iyang mga anak, usahay adunay lalaki nga uban.

copy.bis: Ang viscosity bahin sa kalisod sa pagdagayday sa likido, dili sa kabug-aton niini!

copy.tl: Ang viscosity ay kung gaano kalapot ang isang likido! Sinasabi nito kung gaano kahirap para sa likidong iyan na dumaloy.
copy.bis: Ang viscosity mao ang pagka-baga sa usa ka likido! Kini nag-ingon unsa kalisod para sa likido nga modagayday.

Can our eyes see the whole electromagnetic spectrum?

Nope! The light our eyes can see is only a tiny part of the whole electromagnetic spectrum.
copy.tl:
Nakikita ba ng ating mga mata ang buong electromagnetic spectrum?

Hindi! Ang liwanag na nakikita ng ating mga mata ay maliit na bahagi lamang ng buong electromagnetic spectrum.
copy.bis:
Makita ba sa atong mata ang tibuok electromagnetic spectrum?

Dili! Ang kahayag nga makita sa atong mata gamay ra nga bahin sa tibuok electromagnetic spectrum.

Which vitamin keeps your eyesight clear?

Vitamin A — found in carrots, squash, and malunggay — helps keep your eyesight clear and fights off sickness!
copy.tl:
Anong bitamina ang mabuti sa mata?

Ang bitamina A na matatagpuan sa karot, kalabasa, at malunggay ay tumutulong sa malinaw na paningin at panlaban sa sakit!
copy.bis:
Unsang bitamina ang maayo sa mata?

Ang bitamina A nga makit-an sa karot, kalabasa, ug malunggay nagtabang sa tin-aw nga panan-aw ug pagsukol sa sakit!

copy.tl: Ang bitamina C ay tumutulong sa katawan na labanan ang sakit at pagalingin ang sugat, at makukuha ito sa kahel at iba pang prutas.
copy.bis: Ang bitamina C motabang sa lawas sa pagsukol sa sakit ug pag-ayo sa samad, ug makuha kini sa kahel ug uban pang prutas.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a vitamin deficiency disease, not the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It does not directly support identifying basic needs.

What happens without enough vitamin C?

Long-term lack of vitamin C can cause scurvy, which brings bleeding gums and weakness.
copy.tl:
Ano ang mangyayari kung kulang sa bitamina C?

Kapag matagal na kulang sa bitamina C, maaaring magka-scurvy, na nagdudulot ng dumudugong gilagid at panghihina.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kung kulang sa bitamina C?

Kung dugay nga kulang sa bitamina C, mahimong magka-scurvy, nga maoy hinungdan sa nagdugo nga gilagid ug kaluya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your muscles need vitamin D too. Too little of it can make your arms and legs feel weak and tire quickly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions muscles and a deficiency effect (weakness, fatigue), but it does not describe how the muscular system works (e.g., contraction, movement, coordination with skeletal system). It is a nutritional fact about vitamin D, not an explanation of the system's function.

copy.en:
Does vitamin D help more than bones?

Yes! Your muscles need vitamin D too. Too little of it can make your arms and legs feel weak and tire quickly.
copy.tl:
Vitamin D lang ba para sa buto?

Hindi lang! Kailangan din ito ng kalamnan mo. Kapag kulang, madaling manghina o mapagod ang binti at braso.
copy.bis:
Vitamin D ra ba para sa bukog?

Dili ra! Ang imong mga kaunoran nanginahanglan usab niini. Kung kulang, dali maluya o makapoy ang bitiis ug bukton.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: our bodies make it when sunlight touches our skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make suggestions about the importance of the Sun to living things for a group or class discussion and confirm and record ideas by referring to trustworthy secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a factual statement about the Sun's role in vitamin D production, which is an importance of the Sun to living things. However, the competency requires students to make suggestions for a group/class discussion and to confirm/record ideas by referring to trustworthy secondary sources. The card does not support the skill of making suggestions, discussing, or using secondary sources; it only supplies a related fact.

copy.en:
Why call it the 'sunshine vitamin'?

Vitamin D got that nickname because our bodies make it when sunlight touches our skin!
copy.tl:
Bakit 'sunshine vitamin' ang Vitamin D?

Tinawag itong 'sunshine vitamin' dahil nakukuha natin ito mula sa sikat ng araw!
copy.bis:
Nganong 'sunshine vitamin' ang Vitamin D?

Gitawag kini nga 'sunshine vitamin' tungod kay makuha nato kini gikan sa sidlak sa adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your body needs 13 essential vitamins to stay healthy and strong!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the number of essential vitamins the body needs, which is a nutrition fact. The competency G3-L-6 focuses on identifying basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. Vitamins are not among the listed basic needs and the card does not teach identification of those needs, so it is only related to the topic of food/nutrition.

copy.en:
How many vitamins does your body need?

Your body needs 13 essential vitamins to stay healthy and strong!
copy.tl:
Ilang bitamina ba ang kailangan mo?

Kailangan ng katawan mo ng 13 pangunahing bitamina para manatiling malusog at malakas!
copy.bis:
Pila ka bitamina ang gikinahanglan sa lawas?

Gikinahanglan sa imong lawas ang 13 ka mahinungdanon nga bitamina aron magpabilin nga himsog ug kusgan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your body only needs a tiny bit of each vitamin every day
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses vitamins as a nutrient, which is a component of food, but does not teach the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It does not directly support identifying basic needs.

copy.en: Your body only needs a tiny bit of each vitamin every day — not a lot at all. A mix of fruits and vegetables gives you just the right amount.
copy.tl: Kakaunti lang na bitamina ang kailangan ng katawan araw-araw — hindi kailangang sobra. Sapat na ang iba't ibang prutas at gulay para makuha ang tamang dami.
copy.bis: Gamay ra kaayo nga bitamina ang gikinahanglan sa lawas kada adlaw — dili kinahanglan og sobra. Igo na ang lainlaing prutas ug utanon para makuha ang husto nga sukod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: vitamins aren't 'burned' for energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses vitamins and calories, not photosynthesis or respiration. It provides no information about the processes, raw materials, or products of photosynthesis or respiration.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: vitamins have no calories
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on nutrition (vitamins) but does not address the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It is only loosely related to food as a need.

copy.en:
Why do vitamins have no calories?

Unlike carbs and fats, vitamins aren't 'burned' for energy -- they work as helpers in the body's reactions instead, which is why they have no calories.
copy.tl:
Bakit walang calorie ang bitamina?

Hindi tulad ng carbohydrates at taba, hindi 'sinusunog' ang bitamina para maging enerhiya -- ginagamit ito bilang katuwang sa mga reaksyon ng katawan.
copy.bis:
Nganong walay calorie ang bitamina?

Dili sama sa carbohydrates ug tambok, dili 'sunogon' ang bitamina aron mahimong kusog -- gigamit kini isip katabang sa mga reaksyon sa lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your body just flushes the extra water-soluble kind out through your pee
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions excretion (flushing through urine) but does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, nor does it explain how body systems work together such as digestion and excretion. It only states a fact about vitamin excess and urine, which is not direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your body just flushes the extra water-soluble kind out through your pee
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe how any of the listed human body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. It only mentions excretion via urine, which is not one of the systems named and is not explained in simple terms as a system function.

copy.en:
Does extra vitamins give more energy?

No extra boost! Taking more vitamins than you need won't make you stronger — your body just flushes the extra water-soluble kind out through your pee.
copy.tl:
Nagbibigay ba ng dagdag lakas ang sobrang bitamina?

Wala palang dagdag! Kung uminom ka ng sobrang bitamina, hindi ka lalakas — basta na lang ilalabas ng katawan ang sobra sa pamamagitan ng ihi.
copy.bis:
Naghatag ba og dugang kusog ang sobra nga bitamina?

Wala diayng dugang! Kung moinom ka og sobra nga bitamina, dili ka mokusog — ipagawas ra sa lawas ang sobra pinaagi sa ihi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: iron is a mineral that helps carry oxygen in your blood so your body can make energy, but iron itself is not energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses iron as a mineral versus energy, but does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It does not directly support the competency's definition of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: iron is a mineral that helps carry oxygen in your blood so your body can make energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions iron's role in carrying oxygen in blood, which touches on the circulatory system, but it does not describe how any body system works. It is only a brief factual statement about iron, not an explanation of the circulatory or other systems.

copy.en:
Is iron a form of energy?

No — iron is a mineral that helps carry oxygen in your blood so your body can make energy, but iron itself is not energy.
copy.tl:
Enerhiya ba ang iron?

Hindi — ang iron ay isang mineral na tumutulong dalhin ang oxygen sa dugo para makagawa ng enerhiya ang katawan, pero ang iron mismo ay hindi enerhiya.
copy.bis:
Kusog ba ang iron?

Dili — ang iron usa ka mineral nga motabang dala sa oxygen sa dugo aron makahimo og kusog ang lawas, apan ang iron mismo dili kusog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI) measures eruption size from 0 to 8.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different types of volcanoes found around the world according to their: a. activity b. type of eruption c. location in the crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the VEI scale for eruption size, but the competency requires describing types of volcanoes by activity, eruption type, and crustal location. The VEI scale does not directly support any of those classification criteria.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI) measures eruption size from 0 to 8.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain what volcanoes are and how they are formed
assignedReviews.reason: The card concerns measuring eruption size, not explaining what volcanoes are or how they are formed. It shares the volcano topic but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: The Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI) measures eruption size from 0 to 8. Each step up means 10 times more erupted material!
copy.tl: Ang Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI) ay sumusukat sa laki ng pagsabog mula 0 hanggang 8. Bawat hakbang pataas ay 10 beses na mas malaking inilabas na materyal!
copy.bis: Ang Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI) nagsukat sa gidak-on sa pagsabog gikan 0 hangtod 8. Ang matag lakang pataas nagpasabot og 10 ka beses nga mas daghang materyal!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: scientists watch for warning signs and give alerts
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that scientists watch for warning signs and give alerts, but it does not teach PHIVOLCS alert levels, how to interpret them, or what to do before, during, and after an eruption. It only touches on the general idea of monitoring and alerts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We can't say the exact moment!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss the patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years with family and community members to assess and describe how predictable patterns of eruptions are
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that the exact eruption time cannot be known, which relates to the predictability of eruptions, but it does not discuss patterns of eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years, nor does it involve discussion with family/community members or assessing predictability. It is only a general statement about unpredictability.

copy.en:
When exactly will a volcano erupt?

We can't say the exact moment! But scientists watch for warning signs and give alerts so people can stay safe.
copy.tl:
Kailan eksaktong puputok ang bulkan?

Hindi masasabi ang eksaktong oras! Pero nagbabantay ang mga siyentista ng warning signs at nagbibigay ng alerts para ligtas ang lahat.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a gyud moputok ang bulkan?

Dili masulti ang eksaktong oras! Apan nagbantay ang mga siyentista og warning signs ug naghatag og alerts aron luwas ang tanan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In 1991, Mount Pinatubo erupted and buried Zambales, Tarlac, and Pampanga in thick ash!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use local information or other reliable sources to identify where the nearest active and inactive volcanoes are located and assess the risk of impacts from eruptions to their local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a historical eruption and its impacts (ashfall, roof collapse) but does not guide students to identify nearest active/inactive volcanoes or assess eruption risk to a local community. It shares the volcanic activity topic but provides no direct instructional support for the competency's skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A typhoon made the ash wet and heavy, collapsing roofs.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions effects of an eruption but does not interpret PHIVOLCS alert levels or demonstrate what to do before, during, and after an eruption. It is only tangentially related to volcanic safety.

copy.en: In 1991, Mount Pinatubo erupted and buried Zambales, Tarlac, and Pampanga in thick ash! A typhoon made the ash wet and heavy, collapsing roofs. It was a massive 20th-century eruption!
copy.tl: Noong 1991, sumabog ang Mount Pinatubo at natabunan ng makapal na ash ang Zambales, Tarlac, at Pampanga! Nagka-bagyo kaya nabasa at bumigat ang ash, gumuho ang mga bubong. Isa itong napakalaking pagsabog!
copy.bis: Niadtong 1991, mibuto ang Mount Pinatubo ug gitabonan sa baga nga ash ang Zambales, Tarlac, ug Pampanga! Miabot ang bagyo maong nabasa ug nibug-at ang ash, nangatumpag ang mga atop. Usa kini ka dakong pagbuto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists watch volcanoes using special instruments!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes volcano monitoring instruments (seismometer, gas, ground swelling) but does not mention PHIVOLCS alert levels or what to do before, during, and after an eruption. It shares the broad topic of volcanic activity but does not directly support the competency's specific skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They measure tiny earthquakes with a seismometer
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models or illustrations to explain how movements along faults generate earthquakes and identify and explain which types of faults are most likely to occur in the Philippines and explain why
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions measuring tiny earthquakes, which is tangentially related to earthquakes, but the competency requires using models/illustrations to explain how movements along faults generate earthquakes and identifying fault types in the Philippines. The card does not address fault movements, fault types, or the Philippines, and does not use models/illustrations.

copy.en: Scientists watch volcanoes using special instruments! They measure tiny earthquakes with a seismometer, check the gases coming out, and look for ground swelling — signs that magma is getting close.
copy.tl: Binabantayan ng mga siyentista ang mga bulkan gamit ang espesyal na instrumento! Sinusukat nila ang munting lindol gamit ang seismometer, tinitingnan ang gas na lumalabas, at naghahanap ng pamamaga ng lupa — senyales na papalapit na ang magma.
copy.bis: Gibantayan sa mga siyentista ang mga bulkan gamit ang espesyal nga instrumento! Gisukod nila ang gagmay nga linog pinaagi sa seismometer, gisusi ang gas nga mogawas, ug gitan-aw ang paghubag sa yuta — timailhan nga nagkaduol na ang magma.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It gets its awesome name from the brilliant scientist Alessandro Volta.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a foreign scientist (Alessandro Volta) and a unit named after him, but does not mention any invention. The competency requires identifying a scientist and their invention/s; the volt is a unit of measurement, not an invention. Thus the card only shares the scientist's name and a related unit, without directly supporting the skill of identifying an invention.

copy.en:
Do you know the unit we use to measure voltage?

It is the volt! It gets its awesome name from the brilliant scientist Alessandro Volta.
copy.tl:
Alam mo ba ang yunit na ginagamit natin para sukatin ang voltage?

Ito ay ang volt! Nakuha niya ang napakagandang pangalan nito mula kay Alessandro Volta.
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo ang yunit nga gamiton nato arang sukdon ang voltage?

Mao kini ang volt! Nakuha niini ang nindot nga ngalan gikan sa siyentipikong si Alessandro Volta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Voyager 1 is the farthest human-made object ever!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how modern research about celestial objects uses new space technologies including telescopes and space probes
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a space probe (Voyager 1) but does not explain how modern research about celestial objects uses space technologies such as telescopes and space probes. It only states a fact about the probe's distance and speed.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It has passed beyond our solar system's heliosphere
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to the solar system and a spacecraft, but it does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or discuss their features and composition.

copy.en: Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 is the farthest human-made object ever! It has passed beyond our solar system's heliosphere and keeps travelling away at about 17 kilometres per second.
copy.tl: Inilunsad noong 1977, ang Voyager 1 ang pinakamalayong human-made object ever! Lumampas na ito sa heliosphere ng solar system natin at patuloy na lumalayo sa bilis na 17 kilometro bawat segundo.
copy.bis: Gilunsad niadtong 1977, ang Voyager 1 mao ang pinaka-layo nga human-made object ever! Lapas na kini sa heliosphere sa atong solar system ug nagpadayon sa pagpalayo sa 17 kilometro matag segundo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its radio signal takes more than 20 hours to finally reach Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a radio signal (a form of EMR) and its travel time, but does not describe EMR as energy created by vibrations of charged particles or as transverse waves. It provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Voyager 1 is so far away! Even traveling at the speed of light, its radio signal takes more than 20 hours to finally reach Earth.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions Voyager 1, a spacecraft in the solar system, but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, names of major celestial objects, their main features, or general composition. It is only tangentially related to the solar system.

copy.en: Voyager 1 is so far away! Even traveling at the speed of light, its radio signal takes more than 20 hours to finally reach Earth.
copy.tl: Napakalayo na ng Voyager 1! Kahit kasimbilis ng liwanag ang radyo nitong senyas, umaabot ito ng mahigit 20 oras bago marating ang Earth.
copy.bis: Layo na kaayo ang Voyager 1! Bisan sama kapaspas sa kahayag ang radyo niini nga senyas, mokabat kini ug kapin 20 ka oras una makaabot sa Earth.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Voyager 1 was the very first spacecraft to reach interstellar space, far beyond our Solar System!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions interstellar space and the Solar System but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or discuss their features and composition. It is only tangentially related to the space theme.

copy.en: Voyager 1 was the very first spacecraft to reach interstellar space, far beyond our Solar System!
copy.tl: Ang Voyager 1 ang unang sasakyang-kalawakan na nakarating sa interstellar space, malayo sa ating Solar System!
copy.bis: Ang Voyager 1 mao ang unang barko sa kalawakan nga nakaabot sa interstellar space, layo sa atong Solar System!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The waling-waling orchid is famous for its big, showy flowers
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a single flowering plant's appearance but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups (flowering/non-flowering plants, animal groups, microorganisms). It only mentions a flowering plant, which is a shared vocabulary, not direct instructional support for the classification competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The waling-waling orchid is famous for its big, showy flowers
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a plant part (flowers) but not the outer parts specified in the competency (leaves, roots, stems) nor their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil. It does not support observing or identifying those structures or their functions.

copy.en: The waling-waling orchid is famous for its big, showy flowers in a beautiful pinkish-purple color.
copy.tl: Ang waling-waling ay sikat dahil sa malaki at makulay nitong bulaklak na may kulay lilang-rosas.
copy.bis: Ang waling-waling bantog tungod sa dagko ug bulukon nga bulak nga lila-rosas ang kolor.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the friction of its tips against the ground drags away leaves and litter
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions friction but does not involve planning or carrying out an investigation, nor does it address different surfaces or the size of frictional forces. It only states a simple fact about friction in sweeping.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the friction of its tips against the ground drags away leaves and litter
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions friction but does not demonstrate friction producing heat, nor does it investigate ways of reducing or increasing friction. It only describes friction as the mechanism for sweeping.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When swept, the friction of its tips against the ground drags away leaves and litter
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an object moving due to friction, but it does not explore or demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes or by people (pushing, pulling, rolling, carrying). The sweeping action is not framed as a demonstration of moving objects.

copy.en:
How does a walis tingting sweep up leaves so well?

It’s made from dried coconut leaf midribs! When swept, the friction of its tips against the ground drags away leaves and litter.
copy.tl:
Paano nakakawalis ng maayos ang walis tingting?

Gawa ito sa pinatuyong tingting ng dahon ng niyog! Kapag iwinawalis, ang kuskos ng dulo nito sa lupa ang humahatak sa mga dahon at basura.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pag-silhig sa silhig nga tingting?

Hinimo kini gikan sa giuga nga tingting sa dahon sa lubi! Kon isilhig, ang kuskos sa tumoy niini sa yuta maoy mokuha sa mga dahon ug basura.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: warm-blooded animals can stay active even at night or in cold weather
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a physiological trait (internal heat production) that allows activity in cold/night, but does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment, nor does it involve mimicry or camouflage. It is only tangentially related to animal-environment interaction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because they make their own body heat, warm-blooded animals can stay active even at night or in cold weather.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why warm-blooded animals can be active at night/cold, which is a behavioral/physiological consequence, but it does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It is not directly teaching any of those three characteristics.

copy.en:
Why can warm-blooded animals stay active at night?

Because they make their own body heat, warm-blooded animals can stay active even at night or in cold weather.
copy.tl:
Bakit aktibo pa rin ang mainit-dugong hayop kahit gabi?

Dahil gumagawa sila ng sariling init, ang mga hayop na mainit ang dugo ay nananatiling aktibo kahit gabi o malamig ang panahon.
copy.bis:
Nganong aktibo pa gihapon ang mainiton og dugo nga hayop sa gabii?

Tungod kay naghimo sila sa ilang kaugalingong init, ang mga mananap nga mainiton ug dugo magpabiling aktibo bisan sa gabii o bugnaw nga panahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: shivering makes heat to warm the body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a specific cold-response (shivering) but does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor mention indicators like body temperature, glucose, or blood pressure. It only touches on body temperature indirectly without framing it as homeostasis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: shivering makes heat to warm the body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how homeostasis is maintained through various feedback mechanisms, both positive and negative
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single example of a thermoregulatory response but does not explain feedback mechanisms (positive or negative), how the response is triggered, or how balance is maintained. It lacks the conceptual content of the competency.

copy.en:
Why do we shiver when it's cold?

Warm-blooded animals, including people, shiver in the cold because shivering makes heat to warm the body.
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo nanginginig kapag malamig?

Ang mga hayop na mainit ang dugo, pati tayo, ay nanginginig kapag malamig dahil ang pangangatog ay gumagawa ng init.
copy.bis:
Nganong mangurog ta kung bugnaw?

Ang mga mananap nga mainiton ug dugo, lakip ang tawo, mangurog kung bugnaw kay ang pagkurog naghimo og init.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Warming up heats your muscles and boosts blood flow, which lowers the risk of muscle injuries and strains.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions muscles and blood flow but does not describe how the muscular or circulatory systems work. It is a health/safety tip about warming up, not an explanation of system function.

copy.en:
Why warm up before exercise?

Warming up heats your muscles and boosts blood flow, which lowers the risk of muscle injuries and strains.
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangang mag-warm-up bago mag-ehersisyo?

Ang pag-warm-up ay nagpapainit ng mga kalamnan at nagpapalakas ng pagdaloy ng dugo, kaya nababawasan ang panganib ng pinsala.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga kinahanglan mag-warm-up sa dili pa mag-ehersisyo?

Ang warm-up nagpainit sa mga kaunuran ug nagdugang sa agos sa dugo, nga nagpakunhod sa risgo sa pinsala sa kaunuran.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Warm water is less dense than cold water! Because of this, warm water naturally rises and floats right above colder water.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why warm water rises due to density differences, but the competency focuses on factors affecting object movement such as size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture. Density and temperature are not among the listed factors, so the card does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en: Warm water is less dense than cold water! Because of this, warm water naturally rises and floats right above colder water.
copy.tl: Mas mababa ang densidad ng warm water kaysa sa cold water! Kaya naman, umaangat ito at lumulutang sa ibabaw ng mas malamig na tubig.

Their stinger actually developed from the body part they use to lay eggs!

Bakit ang babaeng putakti lang ang may tibo?

Ang tibo nila ay galing sa bahaging dati'y ginagamit nila sa pangingitlog!

Ang tusok nila naggikan sa parte nga kanhi gigamit nila sa pagpangitlog!

Why do wasps sting?

Mostly to defend themselves or their nest — so the safest thing to do is leave a wasp nest alone.

Bakit tumutusok ang putakti?

Kadalasan para ipagtanggol ang sarili o ang kanilang pugad — kaya ang pinakaligtas ay huwag galawin ang kanilang pugad.
copy.bis:
Nganong motuslok ang putakti?

Kasagaran aron depensahan ang ilang kaugalingon o salag — mao nga ang labing luwas mao ang dili paghilabot sa ilang salag.

Why can a wasp sting again and again?

A wasp has a smooth stinger, so it can sting again and again without dying, but a honeybee can sting only once and dies afterward.

Bakit paulit-ulit na nakakatusok ang putakti?

Ang putakti ay may makinis na tibo, kaya nakakatusok ito nang paulit-ulit nang hindi namamatay, samantalang ang pukyutan ay isang beses lang at namamatay pagkatapos.
copy.bis:
Ngano balik-balik makatuslok ang putakti?

Ang putakti adunay hamis nga tibo, mao nga makatuslok kini og balik-balik nga dili mamatay, samtang ang putyukan usa ra ka higayon ug mamatay human niini.

Why does a wasp sting burn?

A wasp sting feels like fire because the venom triggers pain nerves straight to your brain—it is not actually hot, your body is just tricked!
copy.tl:
Bakit nag-aapoy ang saksak ng putakti?

Parang nasusunog ang katawan kapag nasaksak ng putakti dahil ginigising ng kamandag ang mga ugat na nagpapadala ng sakit sa utak—hindi naman talaga mainit, nililinlang lang ang katawan mo!
copy.bis:
Nganong murag nagdilaab ang tusok sa putyukan?

Murag nagdilaab ang tusok sa putyukan kay ang hilo maglihok sa mga nerbiyos nga magdala og kasakit ngadto sa utok—dili gyud kini init, ang lawas lang gilimbongan!

How hot does water get when it boils at sea level?

It boils at 212 °F (212 degrees Fahrenheit)! That is a lot of heat.
copy.tl:
Gaano kainit ang tubig kapag kumukulo sa antas ng dagat?

Kumukulo ito sa 212 °F (212 degrees Fahrenheit)! Nakakapang-init 'yan.

Unsa ka init ang tubig kung mobukal sa lebel sa dagat?

Mobukal kini sa 212 °F (212 degrees Fahrenheit)! Kaayo ka init niini.

At what temperature does water boil?

At normal pressure, water boils at 100 degrees Celsius, which is also written as 100°C!

Sa karaniwang presyon, kumukulo ang tubig sa 100 degrees Celsius, o 100°C!

Sa unsang temperatura mubukal ang tubig?

Sa normal nga presyon, mubukal ang tubig sa 100 degrees Celsius, o 100°C!

Did dinosaurs drink the same water we drink today?

Yes! The water we drink today is the exact same water that has been cycling on Earth since the time of the dinosaurs.

Uminom ba ang mga dinosaur ng parehong tubig na umiinom natin ngayon?

Oo! Ang tubig na umiinom tayo ngayon ay parehong tubig na umiikot na sa Daigdig mula pa noong panahon ng mga dinosaur.

Nag-inom ba ang mga dinosaur sa parehong tubig nga atong giinom karon?

Oo! Ang tubig nga atong giinom karon mao gihapong tubig nga nagtuyok sa Yuta sukad pa sa panahon sa mga dinosaur.

Sinusukat natin ito sa pamamagitan ng pagtingin kung gaano tumaas ang tubig kapag inilubog ang bato!
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato pagsukod sa volume sa bato?

Gisukod nato kini pinaagi sa pagtan-aw kung pila ka taas ang tubig kung itusmaw ang bato!

Water loves clinging to glass and plastic! In a thin tube, its edges creep up the sides to form a little curve.

Mahilig kumapit ang tubig sa salamin at plastik! Sa manipis na tubo, umaalsa ang gilid nito para gumawa ng maliit na kurba.

Nganong maghimo og kurba ang tubig sa sulod sa salamin?

Ganahan mokupot ang tubig sa salamin ug plastik! Sa nipis nga tubo, mosaka ang kilid niini aron maghimo og gamay nga kurba.

copy.tl:
Ano ang ipinapahiwatig ng 'mata' ng bagyo sa satellite image?

Ang makapal na puting ulap ay senyales ng matinding kondisyon, at ang maliit na butas sa sentro—the eye—ay nagpapakita ng lakas at pagka-organisa ng bagyo.
copy.bis:
Unsay gipasabot sa 'mata' sa bagyo sa satellite image?

Ang makapal nga puting panganod nagpakita sa grabe nga kondisyon, ug ang gamay nga klaro nga buho sa sentro—the eye—nagpakita sa kusog ug organisasyon sa bagyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they give the forecasts and typhoon warnings we see on the news
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that PAGASA provides typhoon warnings, but it does not describe weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal. It only states that warnings are given, not the signal levels or associated conditions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PAGASA runs weather stations all over the country
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions weather stations and forecasts, but it does not involve examining a local weather chart, making interpretations, or describing safety precautions for poor or extreme weather. It is only tangentially related to weather monitoring.

copy.en: In the Philippines, PAGASA runs weather stations all over the country! From their data, they give the forecasts and typhoon warnings we see on the news!
copy.tl: Sa Pilipinas, ang PAGASA ang nagpapatakbo ng mga weather station sa buong bansa! Mula sa datos nila, naibibigay nila ang forecast at babala sa bagyo na nakikita natin sa balita!
copy.bis: Sa Pilipinas, ang PAGASA maoy nagpadagan sa mga weather station sa tibuok nasud! Gikan sa ilang datos, mahatag nila ang forecast ug pasidaan sa bagyo nga atong makita sa balita!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It goes through stages: tropical disturbance, tropical depression, tropical storm, and typhoon!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the life-cycle stages of a tropical cyclone, not the typical weather conditions before, during, and after a cyclone. It does not mention winds, rainfall, pressure, or other weather conditions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It goes through stages: tropical disturbance, tropical depression, tropical storm, and typhoon!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some effects of weather disturbances that occur in or near the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card lists cyclone stages but does not describe any effects of weather disturbances in or near the Philippines, such as flooding, storm surges, or damage.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It goes through stages: tropical disturbance, tropical depression, tropical storm, and typhoon!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card names the stages of typhoon development but does not explain how typhoons develop (e.g., warm ocean water, low pressure) or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons. It also does not involve gathering information from secondary sources.

copy.en:
How does a tropical cyclone grow and end?

It goes through stages: tropical disturbance, tropical depression, tropical storm, and typhoon! It can disappear at any stage if it hits land or ocean conditions change.
copy.tl:
Paano lumaki at nawawala ang isang tropical cyclone?

Dumadaan ito sa yugto: tropical disturbance, tropical depression, tropical storm, at typhoon! Mawawala ito kahit saang yugto kapag tumawid sa lupa o nagbago ang dagat.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagdako ug pagkawala sa tropical cyclone?

Moagi kini sa yugto: tropical disturbance, tropical depression, tropical storm, ug typhoon! Mahanaw kini sa bisan unsang yugto kung motabok sa yuta o magbag-o ang dagat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Concrete and asphalt in cities absorb heat and hold it longer than the soil and vegetation in rural areas.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes heat absorption and retention but does not identify or name conduction, convection, or radiation, nor does it present advantageous/disadvantageous examples of these specific heat transfer modes. It only touches on the general concept of heat, making it related but not directly supporting the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why are cities usually hotter than the nearby countryside?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions temperature difference between city and countryside, which is a weather-related characteristic, but it does not identify the basic weather characteristics listed (air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, cloud cover) nor describe weather patterns. The focus is on urban heat island effect, not on describing weather characteristics.

copy.en:
Why are cities usually hotter than the nearby countryside?

It's the urban heat island effect! Concrete and asphalt in cities absorb heat and hold it longer than the soil and vegetation in rural areas.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mainit ang mga siyudad kumpara sa mga nakapaligid na rural na lugar?

Dahil ito sa urban heat island effect! Ang concrete at asphalt sa siyudad ay nagsisipsip ng init at mas matagal itong tinatago kaysa sa lupa at halaman.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga mas init ang mga siyudad kumpara sa kasikbit nga rural nga lugar?

Tungod kini sa urban heat island effect! Ang concrete ug asphalt sa siyudad nagsupsop sa init ug mas dugay kini gitago kaysa sa yuta ug tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: slightly acidic water dissolves limestone and carves out big caves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes chemical weathering dissolving limestone to form caves, but does not explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals. It shares the broad topic of weathering but provides no direct support for soil formation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: slightly acidic water dissolves limestone and carves out big caves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card illustrates weathering (dissolution) rather than erosion transporting Earth materials. No movement or transport of materials is described, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Over many years, slightly acidic water dissolves limestone and carves out big caves like in Sagada!
copy.tl: Sa maraming taon, ang bahagyang acidic na tubig ay tumutunaw ng limestone at nakakabuo ng malalaking kweba tulad ng sa Sagada!
copy.bis: Sa daghang katuigan, ang tubig nga bahagyang acidic motunaw sa limestone ug makahimo og dagkong langob sama sa Sagada!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Weathering is why old stone statues, churches, and buildings fade and wear down after many years of rain and wind!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes weathering wearing down stone structures, but does not explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals. It shares the weathering topic but gives no direct instructional support for soil formation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Weathering is why old stone statues, churches, and buildings fade and wear down after many years of rain and wind!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The competency concerns changes in material properties due to temperature changes, such as burning wood or coal. The card attributes wear to rain and wind, not temperature, and does not address the stated skill.

copy.en: Weathering is why old stone statues, churches, and buildings fade and wear down after many years of rain and wind!
copy.tl: Ang weathering din ang dahilan kung bakit nakukupas at nasisira ang mga lumang estatwa, simbahan, at gusaling bato matapos ang maraming taon ng ulan at hangin!
copy.bis: Ang weathering usab ang hinungdan ngano nga makupas ug madaot ang mga karaang estatwa, simbahan, ug gambalay nga bato human sa daghang tuig nga ulan ug hangin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: who lays all the eggs for the whole colony
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that a weaver ant queen lays eggs, which is an example of an egg-laying animal. However, the competency requires identifying which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young versus laying eggs (e.g., mammals vs. birds/reptiles). The card does not contrast these groups or help a student classify animals into those categories; it only provides a single isolated fact about ant reproduction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: who lays all the eggs for the whole colony
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions reproduction (laying eggs) as a characteristic of living things, but the competency asks students to describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce. The card does not describe reproduction as a general characteristic, nor does it address growth or response. It only gives a specific fact about ant colony founding, which does not directly teach the competency's skill of describing living things' characteristics.

copy.en: Every weaver ant colony starts with just one queen, who lays all the eggs for the whole colony.

copy.bis: Ang matag kolonya sa hantik magsugod sa usa lang ka rayna, nga mangitlog alang sa tibuok kolonya.

copy.bis: Mas gusto sa weaverbird ang lab-as ug lunhaw nga sagbot kay humok kini ug sayon habihon kaysa sa uga nga sagbot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If you visited a planet with stronger gravity like Jupiter, you would actually weigh more than you do right here on Earth!

assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on gravity and weight but does not identify that forces act between objects or that forces can be measured. It provides no instructional support for the specific competency about forces acting between objects and measurement.

copy.en: If you visited a planet with stronger gravity like Jupiter, you would actually weigh more than you do right here on Earth!
copy.tl: Kung bibisita ka sa planetang may mas malakas na grabidad gaya ng Jupiter, mas mabigat ang magiging timbang mo kaysa dito sa Earth!
copy.bis: Kung mobisita ka sa planetang mas kusog ang grabidad sama sa Jupiter, mas bug-at ang imong timbang kay sa dinhi sa Yuta!
